feedback: Written before this candidate has raced, so no outcome is stated for it. Iteration 8 (mass 0.4 kg, track 0.08 m, kd 0.30, seven sensors at 20 mm, y = 0.07 m, 12 mm footprints, +/-0.06 m span) scored 71.37, the best so far. Mass reduction lifted all three tracks (oval 86.4, s-bend 76.6, slalom 51.1), but max_error still sits at 0.062-0.066 m, just past the fixed floor. Steering oscillation rose on the s-bend and slalom (0.173 and 0.168, against 0.161 at 0.6 kg in iteration 7), so yaw response is now close to its useful limit. Iteration 7 showed that wheel_track narrowing was the only drivetrain change to give a clear gain, and iteration 6 showed that the 16 mm footprint did not help. Depending on the next race: if max_error on the s-bend and slalom falls to about 0.06 m with line_loss_events near 0 and oval progress is only slightly lower, keep wheel_radius 0.025 m. If progress on the oval falls sharply and max_error still sits at 0.06 m or more, the controller response is the limit rather than speed, so return toward 0.0275 m as a compromise. If steering oscillation on the slalom rises above about 0.18, the lower speed is not helping the controller, so restore mass to 0.5 kg.
requested_changes: If the s-bend and slalom still show max_error near 0.062-0.066 m and line_loss_events of 1 at wheel_radius 0.025 m, but oval progress falls by more than about 0.03, try wheel_radius 0.0275 m as the compromise, citing the iteration 8 progress of 0.201 on the oval and 0.188 on the s-bend.
If slalom steering_oscillation rises above about 0.18 with the smaller wheel, set mass to 0.5 kg, citing iteration 8 (0.168 on the slalom at 0.4 kg) against iteration 7 (0.161 at 0.6 kg).

Keep sensor_size at 0.012 m, sensor y at 0.07 m, seven sensors at 20 mm spacing and wheel_track at 0.08 m. Iteration 6 (16 mm footprint) scored lower than iteration 5, and iteration 7 showed the 0.08 m track gave the only clear drivetrain gain.
